For a three-dimensional beam-column joint with beams framing inte the joint in
two different vertical planes (i.e. not all the beams are in the same vertical plane),
the forces acting on the beam-column joint need only be considered in each
vertical plane at a time. In other words, such a three-dimensional beam-column
joint has to be considered twice, each time as a two-dimensional beam-column
joint in a vertical plane containing the beams in the same vertical plane.
N#S3101 states that the forces in each vertical plane may be considered
independently, but in actual fact, the horizontal joint shear force in one vertical
plane could affect the joint shear reinforcement design in the other vertical plane
through the factor C, (see Clauses 11.3.5 and 11.3.6 of N#S3101: Part 1 and

Clauses 6.8.1.5 and 6.8.1.6 of the new code).

The forces acting on a beam-column joint in each vertical plane are:

* axial force N’, horizontal shear force FV. and bending moment MW, from the
column above the joint;

* axial force N", horizontal shear force F,' and bending moment M,' from the
column below the joint;

* vertical shear force MF, and bending moment AM, from the beam al one side
of the joint; and

« vertical shear force F,' and bending moment Jf,’ from the beam at the other
side of the joint, if any.
